answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed on proven fraud, like shale layers that only yield after sustained pressure. Verification acts as a prism: one real-world credential refracts into many unlinkable proofs, so a single person cannot mint a gale of fake agents cheaply. The stake makes each extra identity cost real money, so flooding the network stops paying off.
